household: the Nolans: Johnny, Katie, Francie and Neeley
creator: Betty Smith
address_as_given: a quiet side street in Williamsburg called Bogart Street
notes: Johnny and Katie's first home after their marriage on January 1, 1901; Francie (born December 1901) and Neeley (born December 1902) arrive here. The novel gives no house number; Katie moves the family after Johnny's drinking spree shames her. The novel calls it Williamsburg, while Bushwick Daily places Bogart Street in Bushwick; the real street runs through the East Williamsburg-Bushwick border area, and the point is its midpoint (about 100 Bogart Street).
source_quote: JOHNNY and Katie were married and went to live on a quiet side street in Williamsburg called Bogart Street.
source2_quote: Why, it was on Bogart Street in Bushwick! Johnny had chosen this little side street because of its “thrilling dark sound.”

household: the Nolans: Johnny, Katie, Francie and Neeley
creator: Betty Smith
address_as_given: Lorimer Street, which was still in Williamsburg but almost near where Greenpoint began
notes: Second home: a ground-floor flat with a bathroom, where Katie and Johnny clean the building in return for rent. No number or cross street is given; the point sits on Lorimer north of Metropolitan Avenue, short of McCarren Park, to match 'almost near where Greenpoint began.' The family leaves when Francie is six, after the episode with Aunt Sissy's box of condoms. Brooklyn Magazine (2013) says the Nolans lived longest on Lorimer, which the novel contradicts: they lived longest on Grand Street.
source_quote: I’m heading for Lorimer Street, in East Williamsburg, where the Nolans live until Francie is six years old.
source2_quote: The Nolans slept in their new home on Lorimer Street which was still in Williamsburg but almost near where Greenpoint began.

household: the Nolans: Johnny, Katie, Francie and Neeley (and baby Laurie from 1916)
creator: Betty Smith
address_as_given: a janitor place on Grand Street in Williamsburg; a top-floor flat over a store
geocode_query: Grand Street and Graham Avenue, Brooklyn
notes: The flat with the tree, the roof and the piano, where most of the novel happens; Johnny dies here in 1915 and the family leaves in 1918 when Katie marries McShane (their next home is not placed). The novel names Grand Street but no number. The corner is my inference from a Graham Avenue trolley stopping 'on the corner' and the children spilling onto Manhattan Avenue; Bookpackers puts it at about 650 Grand. Betty Smith herself lived on the top floor of 702 Grand Street, near Graham Avenue (Wikipedia).
source_quote: There are other redeeming qualities to this flat on Grand Street, and the Nolans make it a good home for many years.
source2_quote: Katie found a janitor place on Grand Street in Williamsburg.

household: with her husband Willie Flittman and their children
creator: Betty Smith
address_as_given: a one-family house in Cypress Hills, around Crescent Street, the last stop on the Broadway El
geocode_query: Crescent Street and Fulton Street, Brooklyn
notes: Katie's sister Evy moves the family here, from an earlier unplaced basement flat, because of Willie's drumming; Francie places it for Katie near the Crescent Street stop of the Broadway El. Katie's mother Mary Rommely (one room, later with Sissy) and Aunt Sissy are given no street anywhere in the novel.
source_quote: It's out East New York way-where Brooklyn changes into Queens. It's around Crescent Street, the last stop on the Broadway El.
